messages:
mia: Heads-up — noticed parity gaps across SDKs for auth env vars. Node sample uses `process.env.API_KEY` while Python samples expect `REDWOOD_API_KEY`. Causes a ton of onboarding friction.
anish: ugh, yeah. Which ones are mismatched?
sam: js sdk still reads `API_KEY`; go and dotnet use `REDWOOD_TOKEN`. python and ruby use `REDWOOD_API_KEY`.
mia: exactly. Also expiration/rotation behavior differs: JS client retries once then fails, python rotates automatically if you call `refresh()` from the token provider.
lucy: that explains some of the support tickets where customers rotate keys and their webapp starts 503ing. :facepalm:
mia: proposal: standardize on three env vars across all SDKs: `REDWOOD_API_KEY`, `REDWOOD_ORG`, `REDWOOD_PROJECT`. Support a legacy alias for 6 months: `API_KEY` -> `REDWOOD_API_KEY`.
anish: I like it. Also need a recommended precedence order: CLI config (local profile) > env var > explicit argument to client constructor. Should we document that?
sam: +1. For rotation, can we expose a lightweight metadata header on tokens (key id + created_at + expires_at) so SDKs can surface 'will expire in Xm' warnings?
lucy: yes — we already put key ids in the KMS response. infra-bot: deploy-bot scheduled: auth-service will add token metadata header X-Redwood-Key-Id and X-Redwood-Key-Exp by 2024-08-01.
mia: example change for README (node):
```bash
# new canonical
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_...
export REDWOOD_ORG=acme
export REDWOOD_PROJECT=search
```
```js
// Node sample
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, org: process.env.REDWOOD_ORG });
```
anish: and add fallback logic in SDKs for the alias: `const key = process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY || process.env.API_KEY;` then log a deprecation warning once.
sam: Important: document rotation recipe (CLI + secrets manager). Eg: upload new key, update secrets manager, then perform zero-downtime rotate by issuing an incremental rollout config to the SDKs via env reload. Link: https://redwood.internal/docs/auth/rotation (internal).
lucy: Also add a small helper in our CLI: `rw auth rotate --key-id KEYID --services web,worker` that will update envs in supported deployers (k8s secrets, ecs params, vercel envs).
mia: who owns the SDK changes? I can take node and python if someone picks go + dotnet + ruby.
anish: I'll take go + dotnet. @sam can you own the deprecation plan and the CLI helper?
sam: Yep. I'll open a single umbrella GH issue linking per-sdk PRs and a 6-month deprecation timeline. Will ping legal if we need to communicate externally.
mia: for telemetry we should emit a small event when we detect legacy env var in use (anonymized) so we can measure adoption. devex-bot: note created: ticket #DX-412 to add deprecation telemetry.
lucy: For rotation semantics, recommend SDKs expose an optional `tokenProvider` interface so infra teams can plug in their own secret manager and CRON-based rotation. Example interface in TS: 
```ts
interface TokenProvider {
  getToken(): Promise<string>
  onChange(cb: (token:string)=>void):void
}
```
anish: agree. Also ensure all SDKs honor EOF-safe shutdown when token changes to avoid leaking requests with old tokens.
mia: timeline idea: this week - finalize env var names + precedence. Next 2 weeks - per-SDK PRs. 6 months - remove legacy alias.
sam: I'll draft the umbrella issue today.
lucy: ok. small ask — can docs include a migration checklist for customers with automated secrets rotation? That reduces support load.
mia: yes, I'll start a doc.
devex-bot: Reminder: RFC meeting on Thu 10am to approve naming and rotation plan. :bell:
mia: thanks all — posting the summary and linking GH issues after the meeting.
